name: Medina
tagline: Inside the walls, with the ribat and the great mosque
description: The UNESCO-listed walled old town, entered through gates in the ninth-century ramparts, holding the ribat you can climb for the view over the rooftops, the great mosque and a covered souk that still functions as a market rather than a display. It is the most atmospheric part of Sousse.
bestFor: Stays that want the medina and its monuments at the door
pros: The ribat, the great mosque and the kasbah museum
Souk shopping at genuinely local prices

name: Boujaffar and the Seafront
tagline: The city beach and the promenade north of the medina
description: The long sand beach running north from the medina walls, backed by a promenade, hotels and apartment blocks. It is where the city goes in the evening and where the summer nightlife concentrates, with the beach itself busy through July and August and largely empty the rest of the year.
bestFor: Summer stays that want the beach and the promenade directly outside
pros: Long sand beach and the promenade at the door
Restaurants and summer nightlife along the front
cons: The highest rents in the city, particularly in summer
Quiet and partly shuttered in winter

name: Khezama and the Northern Districts
tagline: Residential blocks between the beach and the highway
description: The residential belt behind the northern beaches, with apartment buildings, local shops, schools and a year-round Tunisian population. Rents here are well below the seafront for a similar flat and the beach remains a ten-minute walk, which makes it the practical choice for a longer stay.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a real neighbourhood ten minutes from the sand
pros: Local shops and markets at ordinary prices
Ten minutes on foot to the beach
cons: Plain apartment blocks with little character

name: Port El Kantaoui (8 km north)
description: A resort built in the 1970s around an artificial marina in a whitewashed Andalusian style, eight kilometres north, with hotels, a golf course and restaurants around the harbour. It is entirely tourist-facing, quieter and cleaner than the city, and empties completely outside the season.
bestFor: Season stays wanting a quiet resort with the city close
pros: Quieter and better maintained than the city
cons: Almost entirely closed from November to April

name: Monastir (20 km south)
tagline: The ribat, the mausoleum and the airport
description: A separate coastal city twenty kilometres south, with a spectacular ribat that has stood in for the Middle East in several films, the Bourguiba mausoleum, a marina and the airport that handles most of the region's charter traffic. It is quieter and cleaner than Sousse and connected by the Metro du Sahel.
bestFor: Stays wanting a calmer coastal base with the airport at hand
pros: The ribat and the mausoleum are genuinely impressive
Light rail connects to Sousse in half an hour
cons: Smaller and quieter, with less going on
